findings.claim: 13.04.02 specifies that a low-confidence price suggestion may render as a wider range with a prominent caveat, which 13.04.03 D-01/DT-01 explicitly forbid and 13.04.02's own D-02 contradicts — two implementers will build opposite surfaces on the exact rendering the confidence model exists to control.
findings.evidence: 13.04.02-pricing-suggestions-repricing.md:53 — `| Partial | Low confidence | Wider range, prominent caveat, or withheld entirely per 13.04.03 |`. Contradicted three ways: (a) 13.04.03-valuation-confidence-thin-market.md:63 DT-01 — "❌ REJECTED: caveats are not read, and the persona least likely to read one (Fan) is the one most likely to be harmed. A caveated number and an uncaveated number are the same number to a non-expert; \"£1,240 (low confidence)\" is remembered as \"£1,240\". Confidence must **gate** the output — change what is shown, not annotate it."; (b) 13.04.03:32 Happy Path step 4 — "Low confidence: raw comps shown as *examples*, no median, no suggestion" and 13.04.03:57 States — `| Partial | Below threshold | Raw comps as examples; no median, no suggestion |`; (c) 13.04.02:77 D-02 — "No confidence, no suggestion — silence over fabrication".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a low-confidence bucket produces (i) a caveated wider range, (ii) raw comps as examples with no suggestion, or (iii) nothing at all. The three options are materially different products for the Fan persona, and the file offers all three in one cell.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A reads 13.04.02's States table and renders '£900–£2,400 (low confidence — based on 2 sales in 6 years)' at the listing price step. Implementer B reads 13.04.03 D-01 and DT-01 and renders no suggestion at all, only two comps as examples. The Fan persona 13.04.03 was written to protect sees an anchored number in build A and none in build B.

findings.claim: gear-marketplace-cx.md gives CX-M11 two different mechanism identities eight lines apart, and routes message-to-disclosure promotion to the wrong cross-cut: messaging is CX-M06 everywhere else in the tree, including inside this domain.
findings.evidence: gear-marketplace-cx.md:382 — `| **Step 6:** Message-to-disclosure promotion | **CX-M11** Messaging & Conversations | DT-12: the highest-volume condition disclosure on any gear marketplace happens in unstructured messages ("any cracks?" → "no, none"). One-tap promotion into structured, timestamped, pack-pinned disclosure...`. Eight lines later, gear-marketplace-cx.md:390 — `| **CX-M11** Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport | Does not serve gear-marketplace. 13.05.02 (live auction bid state) may need it...`. The second name is canonical (13.05.02:71 and 20.05.06 both use it); messaging is CX-M06 in this same domain — 13.05.01:127 "Consumes **CX-M06 Messaging & Contextual Inbox** — conversation around the offer, never the offer itself", 13.06.02:166 "Consumes **CX-M06 Messaging** — order-scoped conversation", 13.12:41 "| Contact / follow | CX-M06 / CX-M28 |".
findings.forcedInvention: Which cross-cut the message-to-disclosure promotion consumes — the real-time audio-transport mechanism named by the ID, or the messaging mechanism named by the label (CX-M06).
findings.failureScenario: An implementer resolving cross-cut dependencies for the domain reads row 382 and adds gear-marketplace to CX-M11's served-domains list for a messaging feature, while row 390 records that CX-M11 does not serve gear-marketplace and would need extending only for live auction bid state. The two rows cannot both be acted on, and CX-M06 — the mechanism that actually hosts the message thread — is never wired to the disclosure promotion at all.

findings.claim: 13.02.02 declares a dependency on CX-M11 for messaging, but CX-M11 is Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport; the messaging mechanism this feature needs is CX-M06.
findings.evidence: 13.02.02-mandatory-flaw-disclosure.md:155 — "- **Consumes CX-M11 Messaging** — DT-12: condition claims made in messages are promotable to structured disclosure." Also 13.02.02:93 — "Free-text is UGC. Routes to moderation (CX-M11/domain 24)." Canonical CX-M11 per 13.05.02-auctions-bidding.md:71 — "Consumes **CX-M11 Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport** — plausibly, for live bid state"; canonical messaging per 13.05.01-offers-counter-offers.md:127 — "Consumes **CX-M06 Messaging & Contextual Inbox**".
findings.forcedInvention: Which mechanism DT-12's one-tap promotion reads from, and therefore which cross-cut must be extended to serve this domain.
findings.failureScenario: The DT-12 promotion path is specified against a real-time audio-transport cross-cut that carries no message thread, so the highest-volume condition-disclosure channel in the domain has no implementable source. Meanwhile CX-M06, which does serve this domain, is never told it must expose a promotable message.

findings.claim: 13.12's Q-02 and Q-03 both argue from the premise that the trader/private regime determination rides on the storefront, which Q-01 in the same table resolves against in terms; the two open questions will be decided from a premise their own file has already retired.
findings.evidence: 13.12-gear-seller-storefront-policies.md:215 Q-01 — "**RESOLVED — domain 01 owns the classification, and it attaches to the party, not the storefront.** Per [01.08 Trader Status Classification]: **D-01** — 'Classification is a party attribute owned by identity, not a listing attribute'... Its **DT-01** rejects DT-05's per-capacity framing head-on... **Consequence for this file**: it consumes and renders the classification...; it never determines it, and **it holds no per-storefront regime field**." Yet :216 Q-02 — "whether the storefront is a first-class object or a view of a principal (DT-05 argues first-class, **because the regime determination needs somewhere to live**)", and :217 Q-03 — "Note DT-05 tilts it: **if the regime determination rides on the storefront**, two storefronts may be the safer model." findings.forcedInvention: Whether the storefront must be a first-class object at all, and whether one principal may hold multiple gear storefronts — both of which the file justifies solely by a regime-carrying role that Q-01 has removed.

findings.claim: 13.05.02 makes bids ascending and binding but never states the minimum bid increment or the permitted auction durations, and no tracked question owns either — an implementer must invent both.
findings.evidence: 13.05.02-auctions-bidding.md:23 — "A timed listing with a start price, optional reserve, and a close time. Bids are ascending and binding. At close, the highest bid above reserve **claims the unit**..." Happy Path step 1 — "Seller lists as an auction with start price, reserve and duration". Nothing in the file, the sub-domain CX, or the index fixes the increment or enumerates durations; the file's three Q rows cover only whether auctions exist at all (Q-01), anti-snipe extension (Q-02) and real-time bid state (Q-03). Contrast the sibling offer feature, which fixes every equivalent constant: 13.05.01 D-06 — "Default expiry **48h**, seller-configurable **24h–7d** per listing... Max **6 moves** per thread".
findings.forcedInvention: The minimum raise over the standing bid (absolute? percentage? band-scaled?) and the set of durations a seller may choose.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A allows any raise above the standing bid, so a £4,000 vintage auction can be won by £0.01 increments and the final seconds become a penny-war; implementer B imposes a 5% increment, which prices a Fan out of a £60 pedal auction in two clicks. Both satisfy 'ascending and binding'.

findings.claim: The 13.05 CX file defers two live product questions with no owner and an expired target, including one — Fan cooling-off on a second-chance offer — that no tracked question in the unit covers.
findings.evidence: 13.05-offers-auctions-negotiation-cx.md:60 — "**Synthesis questions deferred** — Medium confidence... its interaction with sub-domain D-03 **needs Step 5** to confirm the sequencing is airtight: the auction's claim must be fully released before an offer claim can open, or the domain oversells via the recovery path — an ironic failure. **Also open: is a second-chance offer binding on the underbidder (it wasn't a bid), and does the Fan persona need a cooling-off treatment here** given 13.05.02 DT-02's overpaying dynamics?" And :31 — "If the ISO expires with a live offer outstanding, the offer must survive its parent context — an offer's lifetime is its own (13.05.01), not the ISO's. `[PENDING — Step 5]`." The target is expired: 13.05.02 Q-02 and 13.05.03 Q-01 both record "Re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5". The unit's Q rows cover binding on an *accepted offer* (index Q-01) but nothing about a second-chance offer or a Fan cooling-off period.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a second-chance offer binds the underbidder who never placed a bid at that price, and whether the Fan gets a cooling-off window after an auction the file itself says is designed to induce overpaying.
findings.failureScenario: A Fan is outbid at £900 on an instrument they hunted emotionally, the winner ghosts, and a second-chance offer at £900 lands three days later. In one build it is binding on them; in another it is an invitation they may ignore. The persona 13.05.02's Role Lens calls 'most at risk' and 'least able to walk away' gets opposite protection depending on which reading the implementer takes.

findings.claim: 13.07.02's States table specifies an 'estimate' rendering for landed cost that the file's own D-01 and D-02 prohibit, and annotates it as a failure mode rather than removing it — leaving whether the state is implemented unresolved.
findings.evidence: 13.07.02-international-customs-landed-cost.md:55 — `| Partial | Estimated, not guaranteed | Explicit "estimate" framing — and per DT-01, this is the failure mode, not a feature |`. Against D-01 (:80) — "A quoted landed cost is a commitment, not an estimate | Per DT-01 — an estimate is a lie with a disclaimer"; D-02 (:81) — "If a border can't be quoted reliably, don't sell across it | Per DT-01 — the honest alternative to a bad quote is no sale, not a hedged one"; and DT-01 (:61) — "❌ REJECTED: an estimate transfers the risk to the buyer at exactly the moment they cannot assess it, and the Fan persona reads an estimate as a price... **A quoted landed cost must be a commitment** (DDP)... If that is commercially unacceptable, the honest alternative is to **not sell across that border** — not to quote a number that might be a lie."
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the Partial state exists in the built product at all. If D-02 governs, an unquotable border is closed and there is no estimate state; if the States table governs, an estimate renders with framing.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building the checkout state machine from the States table implements a Partial branch that renders 'Estimated import charges — not guaranteed' for a destination whose de-minimis ruleset the platform cannot keep current. D-02 required that border to be closed instead, and DT-01 names this exact rendering as the failure that 'destroys the buyer relationship more thoroughly than almost anything else in the domain'.

findings.claim: The parcel/freight classification envelope — which D-01 makes automatic and silent, and against which a seller override is flagged for abuse review — is stated only approximately, so the classification boundary and the override-abuse test are both untestable as written and no question owns the numbers.
findings.evidence: 13.07.01-freight-oversize-packing.md:25 — "When a listing's catalog model (13.01.01) carries dimensions and weight that exceed the parcel envelope, the item is classified `freight` — not `parcel` — at listing time, silently. The threshold is a physical fact of the carrier network, not a WeJammin policy: **broadly, anything over ~30kg, over ~150cm on the longest side, or palletised**..." The classification is load-bearing for an abuse signal at :51 — "Classification is derived from the catalog model, not free-typed per listing — **an override below the model's known envelope is flagged**, and the parcel-shipped freight item that arrives broken forfeits the packing-standard defence... seller override is logged and surfaced to Trust & Safety (24)". None of the file's three Q rows owns the numbers (Q-01 arrange-vs-broker, Q-02 human-quote checkout, Q-03 where delivery legally ends).
findings.forcedInvention: The exact mass and dimension cut-offs, and therefore the boundary at which an item silently changes transport regime and at which a seller's declaration becomes a flagged override.
findings.failureScenario: A 29kg 2×12 combo is parcel in one build and freight in another. In the parcel build the buyer sees no freight line and no delivery requirements; in the freight build they see a quote that may exceed the amp's value. A seller who declares 28kg on a model whose envelope is '~30kg' is either compliant or flagged to Trust & Safety, with no way to tell which.

findings.claim: 13.09.02 gives three different answers to who authors a consigned listing's disclosure: the Behavior section assigns it to the consignee, an Edge Case treats it as an open question, and D-03 assigns it to the consignor.
findings.evidence: 13.09.02-consignment-sales-custody.md:23 (Behavior) — "Custody transfers; **ownership does not** (sub-domain D-01). **The consignee lists, discloses** (13.02 — on someone else's object), holds, and ships." :40 (Edge Cases) — `| Consignee discloses inaccurately (13.02.02) | The consignor bears the liability for a disclosure they didn't make | **Who signs the disclosure? See DT-01** |`. :79 (Decisions) — `| D-03 | **The consignor signs the disclosure; the consignee transcribes** | Per DT-01 — knowledge and liability must not separate. |`. DT-01 (:59) reasons to D-03's answer — "Either the consignor must sign the disclosure (and the consignee merely transcribes), or the domain's disclosure liability model has an exception it hasn't acknowledged. **The first is correct and needs designing.**"
findings.forcedInvention: Who is in the disclosure UI, who signs the liability-bearing affirmation, and whose account the checklist answers are attributed to on a consigned listing.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer builds the consignment listing flow from the Behavior paragraph and puts the consignee in the disclosure form, since they are the party holding and photographing the instrument. The consignor — who owned it for thirty years and knows about the 1998 headstock repair — never signs, and 13.02.03 D-03's 'the seller signs the disclosure and carries the liability' rule is silently broken for the one selling path DT-01 identified as breaking it.

findings.claim: Two inline deferral markers in 13.09 carry no owner, and one carries no target at all; neither is covered by any tracked question in the unit, unlike the unit's other markers which are.
findings.evidence: 13.09.01-tradein-part-exchange.md:41 — `| Owner trades in gear with an outstanding layaway or lien | They don't fully own it | `[PENDING]` — the chain (13.06.05) would know |` — a bare marker with no owner and no target. 13.09.03-inspection-intake-grading.md:47 — `| Findings contradict a previous owner's disclosure on the chain | The instrument's recorded history is wrong somewhere | Genuinely valuable signal; `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |` — target is the stage 13.09.01 Q-02 records as "the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5". Neither is covered: 13.09.01's Q rows are Q-01 (margin exposure), Q-02 (return shipping) and Q-03 (dealer persona); 13.09.03's are Q-01 (offer goes up), Q-02 (grader distribution) and Q-03 (who grades). Contrast the unit's other two markers, which *are* covered — 13.09.01:38 by its own Q-02, and 13.09.02:38 by its own Q-02.
findings.forcedInvention: What the trade-in flow does when the inbound unit carries an outstanding layaway or lien (block, warn, proceed and record?), and what happens when a bench inspection contradicts a previous owner's chain disclosure.
findings.failureScenario: An owner trades in a guitar still under an active layaway from a previous purchase. The chain knows they do not fully own it, but nothing says whether intake blocks, warns, or proceeds — so one build writes two ownership transfers over an encumbered unit (13.09.01 D-01) and another refuses the trade-in outright.

findings.claim: Two of 13.10's decisions state normative defaults only qualitatively — 'defaults conservative' and 'bounded and short' — and no question owns either number, though both directly determine what a renter sees and how long a deposit is held.
findings.evidence: 13.10.02-rental-availability-reservation.md:79 — `| D-02 | Turnaround buffer is **configurable and defaults conservative** | A unit returned Monday is not rentable Monday; ignoring that guarantees the DT-02 cascade. |` (reinforced at :39 — "Buffer must be configurable and default conservative"). 13.10.03-deposits-damage-return-condition.md:82 — `| D-04 | The assessment window is **bounded and short** | An open-ended window on a unit that goes out again tomorrow makes findings unattributable. |` (:54 — "with a bounded window, not indefinite"; :39 — "Assessment window is minutes at a loading dock, not days"). Neither number is owned by a tracked question: 13.10.02 Q-01 (closed), Q-02 (re-sourcing), Q-03 (8-month escrow); 13.10.03 Q-01 (pooled vs per-unit history), Q-02 (wear/damage line), Q-03 (damage exceeding deposit). Contrast 13.12, which declares its equivalents as numbered seeds ("away mode ≤ 90 days (seed)", "handling time 1–30, default 3 parcel · 10 freight").
findings.forcedInvention: The default turnaround-buffer length and the assessment-window duration.
findings.failureScenario: Build A sets a 1-day turnaround buffer and a 2-hour assessment window; build B sets 3 days and 48 hours. In A a renter can book a unit returning tomorrow and the lender must assess at the dock; in B the same unit shows unavailable for three days and the renter's deposit is held two days after return. Both satisfy 'conservative' and 'bounded and short'.

coverageNote: Enumeration matches the expected 11 units / 65 files exactly. All 65 files were read; the five largest (13.08.01 75KB, 13.03.01 61KB, 13.02.02 58KB, 13.01.02 58KB, 13.12 56KB) were read in full via section extraction rather than as one block. Cross-cutting checks were run programmatically over all 65 files rather than by eye: marker inventory (33 PENDING / 45 OWNER / 32 DEEP), Role Lens and Role Matrix completeness (54 role-bearing files, all four personas present, zero empty cells), open-question well-formedness (215 Q rows, 0 missing an owner or a deferral target), CX-M mechanism-label consistency against the whole ideation tree, and a vague-normative-term sweep across the five largest units. The 215/215 clean Q-row result is why every Dimension 7 finding is a warning rather than a blocking failure: the failure mode is confined to inline and CX-file markers outside the Q tables, and five of the eleven such clusters were already resolved by their own children.
